action.mutates: creates /run/p8test-nmvpn (0700) with a throwaway CA (CN p8test-vpn-ca) and a server key and certificate it signs (CN p8test-vpn-server); copies the CA over the fixture file /etc/p8test-vpn/ca.crt (node fixture p8test_vpn_ca); adds the route 203.0.113.50/32 dev enp0s8

installs openvpn on the peer if absent; adds 203.0.113.50/32 to its enp0s8; writes /etc/p8test-nmvpn (the handed-over CA, server certificate and key, a password check script accepting p8testuser / p8test-vpn-not-a-secret, server.conf: tap, UDP 1194, pool 10.199.0.10-50, AES-256-GCM:AES-256-CBC, comp-lzo, no client certificate); starts the server as a daemon logging to /run/p8test-nmvpn-server.log

outcomes.outcome: the profile file is root-only and NetworkManager loads it as an OpenVPN connection under its name
the loaded profile carries the parameters (remote, CA, VPN user, cipher, password auth, tap)
only the local user may use the connection, and its UUID is stable (fqdn_uuid of the name)
the profile connects to an OpenVPN server with the user's password (a tap address, the server reachable through the tunnel), and a wrong password does not connect
the desktop's own secret agent asking the user for the password when the profile is brought up

uncovered.why: the password is agent-owned (password-flags=1); the exercise supplies it with nmcli's passwd-file, and the runner starts no GNOME session whose agent would ask
